items.title: Show HN: DispatchSEO – open-source SEO manager tool for Claude Code
items.why_it_matters: An indie developer open-sourced DispatchSEO, an SEO manager tool built entirely with Next.js, Supabase, and Claude Code. This is a real-world, working example of your exact stack being used to ship a complex product, complete with a public repository you can study. This week, clone the GitHub repo and look at how they structured their Supabase database and integrated the headless Claude Code builder to automate tasks.

items.title: Agent-Manager: A Tmux TUI for Running Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode
items.why_it_matters: A new open-source terminal tool called Agent-Manager provides a Tmux TUI specifically designed to run and manage multiple Claude Code and Codex sessions simultaneously. If you find yourself waiting on Claude Code to finish a task before you can start another, this lets you run them in parallel without losing track of your terminal windows. This week, install agent-manager via GitHub and use it to run a backend Supabase migration in one pane while generating a Next.js component in another.

items.title: Show HN: Agentic – Run Claude Code on different models with routing and budgets
items.why_it_matters: An open-source tool called Agentic was released that allows you to run Claude Code commands but route the actual LLM requests to cheaper alternative models like DeepSeek or Mistral while keeping budgets in check. Since you use Claude Code daily, this directly addresses the high token costs of running Sonnet 3.5 for simpler coding tasks. This week, install Agentic, configure it with a cheap DeepSeek API key, and use it to write your next basic Next.js utility function to see how much you save.

items.title: I aggregated 32 Claude Code sessions: 96.8% of tokens went to re-reading history
items.why_it_matters: An analysis of 32 Claude Code sessions revealed that a massive 96.8% of all tokens consumed are spent on the model re-reading the command history rather than generating new code. This means long, continuous sessions are quietly draining your API budget on redundant context. This week, make it a habit to exit and restart your Claude Code CLI session whenever you transition from one distinct task (like setting up a Supabase table) to another (like styling a Next.js page).

items.title: Show HN: Ski – Voice Coding for Claude Code, Codex and More – On-Device – Free
items.why_it_matters: Ski is a new, free, on-device voice coding application built specifically to work with agents like Claude Code and Codex. Instead of typing out long prompts to direct your AI, you can speak naturally, and Ski transcribes and passes the instructions directly to your active coding agent. This week, download the Ski desktop app and try dictating your next feature request to Claude Code instead of typing it.

items.title: Show HN: Burnless makes LLM context a protocol. Token savings are a side effect
items.why_it_matters: A new open-source tool called Burnless acts as a context protocol to stop LLMs from burning tokens on historical conversation data that is no longer needed for the next step. By separating execution from memory, it helps keep your API costs down without sacrificing model performance. This week, check out the Burnless GitHub repo and try integrating it into your AI-ingest backend to prune unnecessary tokens from your news-filtering prompts.
